name: Basic Electronics Engineering Lab
objectives: To introduce hands-on descriptions of various physical and analytical concepts of electronic devices such as diodes, transistors, operational amplifiers and logic gates and their applications.
outcomes: Understand characteristics of various circuits using diode.
Analyze characteristics of various circuits using BJT.
Analyze characteristics of various circuits using FET.
Implement various logic gates and verify their truth-tables.
Improve skills of team work, technical communication and report writing.
rule: All experiments (manuals and handouts available in the lab)
note:
Record format: aim, components with type numbers (e.g. IN4007, BC547, 7400), circuit diagram, observation tables, graph paper plots and result; mark the pin diagram of every device.
Check the polarity, supply level and ground before power-on; test diodes and transistors with a multimeter first, and keep the function generator amplitude low.
Examiners ask for the working point, the region of operation and what each graph tells you; learn one line for each curve on your graph.

exps.title: To determine and plot V-I characteristics of P-N junction in both forward bias and reverse bias
exps.aim: Plot the diode characteristics, and find the knee voltage, dynamic resistance and reverse saturation current.
exps.apparatus: PN diode (IN4007), DC supply, resistor, voltmeter, milliammeter, microammeter, breadboard
exps.formula: I = I₀(e^{V/ηV_T} − 1), V_T = kT/q ≈ 26 mV at 300 K; dynamic resistance r_d = ΔV/ΔI.
viva: What is the cut-in voltage of Si and Ge diodes?
About 0.7 V for silicon and 0.3 V for germanium.
Why is reverse current very small?
Only minority carriers flow; the depletion region blocks majority carriers.
What is dynamic resistance?
The ratio of small change in voltage to change in current, r_d = ΔV/ΔI, at a given operating point.

exps.title: To determine and plot the wave shapes of clipping and clamping circuits
exps.aim: Observe how diode circuits clip a waveform at a level or shift its DC level.
exps.apparatus: Signal generator, CRO, diodes, resistors, capacitor, DC bias source
exps.formula: Clipper limits the output to the diode threshold plus the bias; a clamper shifts the waveform by about the peak value without changing its shape.
viva: What is the difference between a clipper and a clamper?
A clipper removes part of the waveform; a clamper adds a DC level but keeps the shape and peak-to-peak value.
Why is the RC time constant of a clamper large?
So that the capacitor holds its charge during the cycle, keeping the DC shift steady.
What does a series positive clipper do?
It removes the positive half cycle (or the part above the reference level).

exps.title: To determine the ripple in the output of a half wave and a full wave rectifier at different loads
exps.aim: Measure the DC and AC output, and calculate the ripple factor with and without a filter.
exps.apparatus: Transformer, diodes, load resistors, capacitor, CRO, multimeter
exps.formula: γ = V_rms(ac)/V_dc; half wave 1.21, full wave 0.482; V_dc = V_m/π (HW), 2V_m/π (FW).
viva: What is the ripple factor?
The ratio of the RMS value of AC component to the DC value in the output.
What is the ripple frequency of a full wave rectifier?
Twice the input frequency (100 Hz for a 50 Hz supply).
What are the maximum efficiencies of HW and FW rectifiers?
40.6 % for half wave and 81.2 % for full wave.

exps.title: To determine and plot V-I characteristics of Zener diode in both forward bias and reverse bias
exps.aim: Plot Zener characteristics and find the breakdown voltage and dynamic resistance in the breakdown region.
exps.apparatus: Zener diode, DC supply, series resistor, voltmeter, milliammeter
exps.formula: Regulator: R_s = (V_in − V_Z)/(I_Z + I_L); Zener dynamic resistance r_z = ΔV_Z/ΔI_Z.
viva: In which bias is a Zener diode used as a regulator?
Reverse bias, in the breakdown region, where voltage stays nearly constant.
What are the two breakdown mechanisms?
Zener breakdown (below about 5 V) and avalanche breakdown (above about 5 V).
Why is a series resistor needed?
It limits the current below the maximum power rating of the diode.

exps.title: To determine and plot input and output characteristics of NPN and PNP bipolar junction transistors in common emitter and common base mode
exps.aim: Plot the input and output characteristics and find h-parameters, α and β.
exps.apparatus: BJT (BC547 or BC557), DC supplies, resistors, voltmeters, ammeters
exps.formula: β = I_C/I_B, α = I_C/I_E, β = α/(1 − α); input resistance = ΔV_BE/ΔI_B; output resistance = ΔV_CE/ΔI_C.
viva: How is the transistor biased in the active region?
The emitter-base junction is forward biased and the collector-base junction is reverse biased.
Which configuration has the highest power gain?
Common emitter, with a large current gain β and a large voltage gain (common collector has a similar current gain 1 + β but no voltage gain).
Why is the base made thin and lightly doped?
So that most of the injected carriers reach the collector without recombining in the base.

exps.title: To determine and plot input and output characteristics of a field-effect transistor
exps.aim: Plot drain and transfer characteristics of a JFET and find pinch-off voltage, I_DSS and g_m.
exps.apparatus: JFET (BFW10), DC supplies, voltmeters, milliammeter, resistors
exps.formula: I_D = I_DSS(1 − V_GS/V_P)²; g_m = ΔI_D/ΔV_GS; r_d = ΔV_DS/ΔI_D; μ = g_m r_d.
viva: What is pinch-off voltage?
The gate-source voltage V_P at which the channel closes and I_D falls to zero; with V_GS = 0 the drain current saturates once V_DS reaches |V_P|.
Why does a JFET have high input impedance?
The gate-channel junction is reverse-biased, so gate current is very small.
Is a JFET bipolar or unipolar?
Unipolar; only one type of carrier carries current.

exps.title: To determine and plot input and output characteristics of a metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor
exps.aim: Plot drain and transfer characteristics of a MOSFET and find the threshold voltage and transconductance.
exps.apparatus: MOSFET (n-channel enhancement), DC supplies, voltmeters, ammeter, resistors
exps.formula: Saturation: I_D = k(V_GS − V_T)²; g_m = ΔI_D/ΔV_GS.
viva: What is the threshold voltage?
The minimum gate-source voltage that forms a conducting channel in an enhancement MOSFET.
Why is the gate current nearly zero?
The oxide layer insulates the gate from the channel.
How do enhancement and depletion MOSFETs differ?
An enhancement device conducts only after the gate voltage induces a channel; a depletion device has a built-in channel.

exps.title: To determine and plot the frequency response of an amplifier
exps.aim: Measure gain over a range of frequencies and find the half-power points and bandwidth.
exps.apparatus: CE amplifier, function generator, CRO, DC supply, resistors and capacitors
exps.formula: Gain (dB) = 20 log₁₀(V_o/V_i); bandwidth BW = f_H − f_L, at the −3 dB (0.707 × mid-band gain) points.
viva: What is bandwidth?
The frequency range between the lower and upper 3 dB (half-power) frequencies.
Why does gain fall at low frequencies?
The coupling and bypass capacitors present higher reactance.
Why does gain fall at high frequencies?
Transistor junction capacitances and stray capacitances shunt the signal.

exps.title: Realization and verification of the truth table of various logic gates
exps.aim: Verify the truth tables of AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR and XNOR gates using ICs.
exps.apparatus: Gate ICs (7408, 7432, 7404, 7400, 7402, 7486), logic trainer kit, LEDs, +5 V supply
exps.formula: Y = A·B (AND), A + B (OR), A′ (NOT), (A·B)′ (NAND), (A + B)′ (NOR), A ⊕ B (XOR).
viva: Which gates are universal?
NAND and NOR, since any Boolean function can be built from either.
What is the output of an XOR gate?
High when the inputs differ, low when they are the same.
What voltage level does TTL use for logic 1?
About 2 V to 5 V; logic 0 is 0 to 0.8 V.

exps.title: Realization and verification of the basic logic gates using NAND and NOR gates
exps.aim: Build NOT, AND and OR gates using only NAND or only NOR gates and verify their truth tables.
exps.apparatus: NAND IC 7400, NOR IC 7402, logic trainer kit, LEDs, +5 V supply
exps.formula: NAND: NOT = (A·A)′, AND = ((A·B)′)′, OR = (A′·B′)′. De Morgan: (A + B)′ = A′·B′.
viva: How do you make a NOT gate from a NAND gate?
Tie both inputs together; then Y = (A·A)′ = A′.
State De Morgan's theorems.
(A + B)′ = A′B′ and (AB)′ = A′ + B′.
Why are NAND gates called universal?
Every logic function can be made from NAND gates alone.

exps.title: To design inverting and non-inverting amplifier using op-amp
exps.aim: Build both op-amp amplifiers and verify their gains for different resistor ratios.
exps.apparatus: IC 741 op-amp, ±12 V supply, resistors, function generator, CRO
viva: What is a virtual ground?
In an inverting amplifier, the inverting input is at almost 0 V because of the very high open-loop gain.
What are the ideal op-amp properties?
Infinite gain, infinite input impedance, zero output impedance and infinite bandwidth.
Why is negative feedback used?
It stabilises the gain, widens the bandwidth and reduces distortion.
